query: Help me understand what's worth analyzing in these travel-expense records.

per_column.name: asset_category
per_column.rationale: Categorizes CI/description into asset types (hardware_endpoint, travel_item, cloud_service), giving a genuine grouping axis for expense analysis. Values are well-grounded readings of the ci/short_description text.

per_column.name: asset_form_factor
per_column.rationale: Adds finer granularity (laptop, desktop, server, vehicle) derivable from CI strings like 'Dell Latitude'/'OptiPlex Desktop'. NULLs for silent rows are acceptable. Some inference (AWS EC2 -> server form factor) is reasonable.

per_column.name: ci_brand_family
per_column.rationale: Extracts brand (dell, hp, apple, cloud_provider) directly from CI text, enabling vendor-level spend grouping. Grounded and only mildly redundant with asset_category.

per_column.name: procurement_action_type
per_column.rationale: Distinguishes new_acquisition vs registration_tracking vs rental from short_description phrasing. Useful classification, though the new_acquisition/registration_tracking split for near-identical 'new hardware asset' vs 'automated creation' descriptions looks somewhat arbitrary and weakly grounded.

per_column.name: has_source_id
per_column.rationale: A bare boolean presence flag that is trivially derivable from an existing original column (source_id). Adds little analytical leverage, but values are exactly grounded.

per_column.name: has_processing_lag
per_column.rationale: Derived from opened_at vs processed_date; a genuine derived signal that could flag delayed processing. Grounded (NaN processed_date -> False is sound), though the lag threshold is opaque.

per_column.name: department_group
per_column.rationale: Rolls up the original department column into groups, a useful aggregation axis. Mapping is plausible but not verifiable from the sampled source text, and it is largely a restatement of an existing original column.

judge.rationale: Most added columns give real grouping axes (asset_category, form_factor, brand_family, procurement action, department_group) useful for understanding travel-expense records and are soundly grounded in the ci/short_description text. has_source_id is a trivial presence flag on an existing column, and procurement_action_type/department_group show some weakly warranted mapping, lowering the aggregate. No clear hallucinations observed; NULL handling for silent rows is appropriate.
